verdict.summary: Core Georgian franchise remains highly profitable (9M26 group net profit GEL 1,155m, +12% YoY; Q3 record GEL 404m; ROE 23.4%) with Fitch BB Stable rating. However, group NPL rose to 3.3% due to acute credit stress in the Uzbekistan digital lending arm (11.8% NPL, 10.8% CoR) alongside shareholder payouts (GEL 1.75/sh quarterly dividend + GEL 50m buyback).

positives: Strong Georgian core profitability: Q3 2026 record net profit GEL 404m (+10% YoY); 9M26 GEL 1,155m (+12% YoY) at 23.4% ROE.
Solid NBG regulatory capital cushions (FY24 standalone CET1 16.8%, Total CAR 23.8%) and Fitch BB Stable rating.
Leading Georgian market duopoly alongside Bank of Georgia.
negatives: Uzbekistan asset-quality deterioration: Uzbekistan segment NPL jumped to 11.8% with 10.8% cost of risk in 3Q26 on vintage seasoning and tighter regulation.
Rising group NPL ratio (3.3% at 3Q26 vs 2.2% FY24) despite Georgian core stability.
Capital returns (GEL 50m buyback + quarterly dividends) while funding high-growth Uzbek digital banking.

background.business_overview: FTSE-250 UK HoldCo owning JSC TBC Bank (co-leading Georgian universal bank) and TBC Uzbekistan (digital consumer bank & Payme).
background.asset_perimeter: Georgian core universal bank + TBC Bank Uzbekistan digital ecosystem.
background.ownership_governance: London Stock Exchange listed; EBRD/IFC historical institutional backing.
